title: Capacitance, inductance and power
blurb: Say what capacitors and inductors store, write kHz and MHz correctly, define impedance, and calculate DC power.

T5C01.why: A capacitor holds energy in the **electric field** between its plates. That ability is capacitance.

T5C02.trap: Henry is inductance, ohm is opposition, volt is voltage.

T5C03.why: A coil holds energy in a **magnetic field**. That ability is inductance.
T5C03.trap: Capacitance uses an electric field, not a magnetic one.

T5C04.trap: Farad is capacitance. Coulomb is a unit of charge.

T5C05.why: Impedance is opposition to AC, so like resistance it is measured in **ohms**.
T5C05.trap: Volts, amperes and coulombs measure voltage, current and charge.

T5C06.why: Kilo is lowercase **k**, then Hz with a capital H: **kHz**.
T5C06.trap: Capital K and lowercase h or z are all wrong.

T5C07.why: Mega is a capital **M**, then Hz: **MHz**.
T5C07.trap: Lowercase m means milli, so mHz is thousandths of a hertz.

T5C08.why: Power is voltage times current: **P = I × E**.
T5C08.trap: A squared current goes with resistance (I² × R), not volts.

T5C09.trap: 23.8 adds the numbers and 0.7 divides them. Power multiplies.

T5C10.trap: 14.5 adds the numbers. Power multiplies volts by amperes.

T5C11.trap: 0.1 divides the wrong way round, and 132 adds the numbers.

T5C12.why: Impedance is the **opposition to AC current flow**: resistance and reactance combined, in ohms.
T5C12.trap: It's the opposition itself, not an inverse of anything.
